anomalies_df_sorted = anomalies_df.sort_values(by=['cmdb_id', 'kpi_name', 'timestamp']).copy()

# Identify consecutive anomaly points by checking timestamp difference
# Assuming metrics are collected at regular intervals, e.g., 60 seconds
# We consider consecutive if the difference between timestamps is <= 60 seconds
anomalies_df_sorted['timestamp_diff'] = anomalies_df_sorted.groupby(['cmdb_id', 'kpi_name'])['timestamp'].diff().fillna(0)

# Mark start of new fault sequences where timestamp difference is greater than 60 seconds
anomalies_df_sorted['new_fault'] = anomalies_df_sorted['timestamp_diff'] > 60

# Assign fault group ids by cumulative sum of new_fault flags
anomalies_df_sorted['fault_group'] = anomalies_df_sorted.groupby(['cmdb_id', 'kpi_name'])['new_fault'].cumsum()

# Aggregate faults by component, KPI, and fault group
faults_agg = anomalies_df_sorted.groupby(['cmdb_id', 'kpi_name', 'fault_group']).agg(
    start_time=('datetime', 'min'),
    end_time=('datetime', 'max'),
    max_value=('value', 'max'),
    max_threshold=('p95_threshold', 'max'),
    count=('value', 'size')
).reset_index()

# Filter out isolated spikes (count == 1)
faults_agg = faults_agg[faults_agg['count'] > 1]

# Filter out faults where max threshold breach is <= 50% of the extremal value
# i.e., (max_value - max_threshold) > 0.5 * max_value
faults_agg = faults_agg[(faults_agg['max_value'] - faults_agg['max_threshold']) > 0.5 * faults_agg['max_value']]

# Prepare final fault summary with relevant columns
